name: Smoked milkfish [tinapang bangus]
definition: Milkfish Chanos chanos smoked whole or butterflied, sold chilled or frozen; tinned smoked milkfish is J2.4 (P3).
reason: Fish-and-smoke kind like smoked haddock (J2.2 axis); page must show smoked milkfish or smoked bangus sold as a product.

name: Tinned saury [sanma; saira]
definition: Pacific saury Cololabis saira packed in a sealed tin, in oil, its own juice or a sauce such as kabayaki.
reason: Species kind in J2.4; sauce in a sealed tin is pack medium (P3). Page (or the Time Out Tokyo one) must show a saury tin.

name: Dried filefish [jwipo]
definition: Filefish (Monacanthidae) fillets dried, plain or lightly seasoned and pressed, sold to eat or to grill.
reason: Dried fish named by species, sold as its own product (Korean jwipo); step 3 keeps seasoned dried fish a grocery. Page must show dried filefish.

name: Dried cuttlefish
definition: Cuttlefish (Sepia) dried whole, in pieces or shredded; dried squid is J2.3.05.
reason: Cuttlefish is a different animal from squid, and Chinese dried classes price it apart. Page must name dried cuttlefish.

name: Fish floss [yu song]
definition: Fish cooked, shredded and dry-fried with light seasoning into a fine dry floss; a blend led by seaweed, sesame or flour is a J5 topping.
reason: Dried fish stays a grocery when seasoned (step 3 note). Page must show fish floss with fish as the main ingredient.

name: Kilka [килька]
reason: Regional name for tinned small clupeids (Baltic sprat, Caspian Clupeonella), usually in tomato: C11 named form; J2.4.09 wording widened.

name: Tinned cod liver [pechen treski]
definition: Cod liver cooked and packed in its own oil in a sealed tin; cod flesh is J2.4.19, cod liver oil H2.
reason: An organ product sold and compared apart from cod flesh (HV_J2_NK2 caveat; Shtil cannery). Page must show tinned cod liver.

name: Tinned hake [merluza]
definition: Hake (Merluccius) packed in a sealed tin or jar.
reason: Species kind in J2.4, same test as DPW1's tinned cod. Page must show a hake tin.

name: Tinned sea bass [lubina]
definition: European sea bass Dicentrarchus labrax packed in a sealed tin or jar.
reason: Sold under its species name (Alalunga). Page must show a sea bass tin.

name: Salt-dried tuna loin [mojama]
definition: Tuna loin salted and air-dried, sold whole or sliced; Mojama de Barbate and de Isla Cristina are named forms (JC1).
reason: A cured form no kind covers (C11: generic label, regional word as synonym). Page must show mojama on sale.
Raw Trachurus is already in the scad kind's definition; tinned horse mackerel goes to J2.4.24.

name: Siberian sturgeon caviar [Baerii]
definition: Roe of the Siberian sturgeon Acipenser baerii, sold as grain caviar.
reason: J2.5.1 kinds go by source species (J-5, CITES code BAE); baerii is not osetra. Page (or Costco Uraqi) must name A. baerii.
Midye dolma: mussels filled with spiced rice. Filled seafood is prepared (P-P, K-45).

name: Tinned jack or horse mackerel [jurel; maasbanker]
definition: Jack or horse mackerel (Trachurus) packed in a sealed tin; Scomber mackerel is J2.4.07.
reason: Trachurus is the scad family and is sold apart from caballa (Chile, Peru, Sri Lanka). Turkey, Captain and Efuta pages show it.

name: Tinned whelk or conch [golbaengi]
definition: Sea snails (whelk, conch) cooked and packed in a sealed tin.
reason: The tinned version of J2.1.3.07; no URL given. Page must show a whelk or conch tin. Golbaengi claim is from memory (†).

name: Tinned sturgeon
definition: Sturgeon flesh (Acipenseridae) packed in a sealed tin; its roe is J2.5.1.
reason: EcoFood tins sold under the species name. Page must show a sturgeon tin.

name: Tinned trout
definition: Trout (Oncorhynchus, Salmo) packed in a sealed tin, smoked or not.
reason: Species kind in J2.4. Page must show a trout tin.

name: Tinned whitefish [sig]
definition: Whitefish (Coregonus) packed in a sealed tin.
reason: Coregonus is a species group, not generic white fish. EcoFood (Sevan) page must show it.

name: Hybrid sturgeon caviar
definition: Roe of farmed sturgeon crosses (Huso dauricus x Acipenser schrenckii, Huso huso x A. ruthenus and others), sold as grain caviar; the cross is the scientific_name.
reason: CITES codes hybrids apart and sellers price them below pure species. Page must name a cross (OLMA's Beluga Hybrid page also shows one).

name: Tinned oysters
definition: Oysters, often smoked, packed in oil or water in a sealed tin.
reason: J2.4 has no oyster kind (tinned clams is J2.4.14). Page must show tinned oysters.

name: Tinned abalone
definition: Abalone (Haliotis, including paua) cooked and packed in a sealed tin.
reason: Sold and gifted as its own product; fresh and dried abalone are J2.1.3.06 and J2.3.08. Page must show tinned abalone.
US north-east 'conch' is channeled or knobbed whelk (Big G: conch and whelk); C9 alias. Queen conch is on no fetched page: no row.

name: Geoduck
reason: Panopea clam sold by name: species of a mollusc kind go below kind (memo 4b). Not maker-bound.

name: Rockfish [ocean perch; redfish]
definition: Raw rockfish or redfish of the genus Sebastes, sold whole or as fillets.
reason: No finfish kind covers Sebastes. Page must show rockfish, redfish or ocean perch sold as a product.
